record.title: Exact Berge-book Turán conjecture in the large-book regime
record.statement:
Let $r$ and $t$ be integers, and let ${\mathrm{ex}}_r(n,\operatorname{Berge-}B_2)$ denote the maximum number of hyperedges in an $r$-uniform $n$-vertex hypergraph containing no Berge copy of $B_2$. **The large-book exact Berge-book Turán conjecture.** If $t>r-2$ and $n$ is large enough, then

$$
{\mathrm{ex}}_r(n,\operatorname{Berge-}B_2)=\frac{n^2}{4(r-1)}+(t-1)^2.
$$

The claim appears in the concluding remarks as a proposed exact improvement based on the paper's constructions, and no proof or disproof is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, “The Turán number of Berge book hypergraphs”, arXiv:2111.11162 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.11162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

record.title: The p-distinguished involution conjecture
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weyl group with $p$-canonical basis $\{c_w\}$ and left $p$-cells. For $w,x,y\in W$, let $\mu_{w,x}^y$ be the coefficient of $c_y$ in $c_wc_x$, and let $h_x^y$ be the coefficient of $H_y$ in the standard-basis expansion of $c_x$. For a Laurent polynomial $f$, write $\operatorname{val}(f)$ for its smallest exponent with nonzero coefficient.

**The p-distinguished involution conjecture.** In each left $p$-cell there is a unique involution $d$ such that

$$
-\operatorname{val}(\mu_{d,d}^d)\geq \operatorname{val}(h_d^1).
$$

This is presented as a conjectural analogue of distinguished involutions for $p$-cells. The paper notes that the theory of $p$-distinguished involutions is not fully developed.
record.source_name: Ben Elias, Lars Thorge Jensen and Joel Gibson, “Categorical diagonalization and p-cells”, arXiv:2111.12190 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.12190

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2021). “This conjecture was proven in type $A$ in .”

record.title: Improved upper bound for feedback vertex sets in graphs of even degeneracy
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an even degeneracy bound, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph of degeneracy $k$. Write $f$ for the size of a minimum feedback vertex set of $G$.

There is an $varepsilon>0$ such that

$$
f\leq \left(\frac{k}{k+2}-\varepsilon\right)n.
$$

The paper gives an easy upper bound with coefficient $\frac{k}{k+2}$ and constructs non-trivial lower bounds, but does not essentially improve this upper bound; the conjecture asserts that a uniform improvement is possible.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Feedback vertex sets in (directed) graphs of bounded degeneracy or treewidth”, arXiv:2111.14986 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14986

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

record.title: Akbari–Alazemi–Andjelić energy bound conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_N$, energy $\mathcal{E}(G)=\sum_{i=1}^N|\lambda_i|$, matching number $\mu(G)$, and largest vertex degree $\Delta$. 

**Akbari–Alazemi–Andjelić conjecture.** The inequality

$$
\mathcal{E}(G)\leq 2\mu(G)\sqrt{\Delta}
$$

holds for any connected graph $G\not\cong C_3,C_5,C_7$ with $\Delta\in\{2,3,4,5\}$.

The conjecture extends a theorem proving the bound for connected graphs with $\Delta\geq 6$. It is refuted: the paper constructs two infinite families of counterexamples.
record.source_name: Đorđe Stevanović, Ivan Damnjanović and Dragan Stevanović, “Finding counterexamples for a conjecture of Akbari, Alazemi and Andjelić”, arXiv:2111.15303 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.15303

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2021). “Finally, Section 4 shows that two families of graphs, inspired by the structure of the majority of small counterexamples, represent infinite families of counterexamples for Conjecture AAA.”

record.title: Generalized large-girth conjecture for strong edge-coloring of regular bipartite graphs
record.statement:
For each integer $k\ge 3$, let $g_k$ be a proposed girth threshold. Let $G$ be a bipartite graph of girth at least $g_k$, maximum degree $k$, and with $m$ edges. A **generalized large-girth conjecture.** There exists a girth $g_k$ such that $G$ satisfies $'_s(G)\le 2k$ and has a strong edge-coloring with colors $1,\ldots,2k$ in which color $2k$ is used on at most

$$
m-(2k-1)\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2k-1}\right\rfloor
$$

edges. The statement slightly weakens the cubic large-girth assertion and generalizes it to maximum degree $k$; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, “Strong Edge-Coloring of Cubic Bipartite Graphs: A Counterexample”, arXiv:2112.01443 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01443

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: The edge clique cover conjecture for graphs with independence number two
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n$ vertices. A **clique** is a set of vertices inducing a complete graph, and the **edge clique cover number** $ecc(G)$ is the minimum number of cliques such that both endpoints of every edge lie in at least one of them. Write $balpha(G)$ for the independence number of $G$. **Edge clique cover conjecture.** If

$$
\alpha(G)=2,
$$

then

$$
ecc(G)\leq n.
$$

This conjecture is a special case of the question whether every claw-free graph satisfies $ecc(G)\leq n$. Positive results were known for claw-free graphs with independence number greater than two, leaving the case $\alpha(G)=2$ as the conjectural case considered here.
record.source_name: Frank Ramamonjisoa, “Edge Clique Covers in Graphs with Independence Number Two: a Special Case”, arXiv:2112.03961 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Stark phase unit conjecture for SIC fiducials
record.statement: Let $d=n^2+3=p$ be a prime in the specified sequence, let $K$ be the real quadratic field used in the construction, and let $e^{i\vartheta_j}$ be the phases in the almost-flat fiducial formula. **Stark phase unit conjecture.** The numbers $e^{i\vartheta_j}$ are Galois conjugates of Stark units for one of the two small ray class fields, and are therefore called Stark phase units. This hypothesis is the number-theoretic ingredient proposed to construct the fiducial vector from Stark units; the source treats it as conjectural.
record.source_name: Marcus Appleby, Ingemar Bengtsson, Markus Grassl, Michael Harrison and Gary McConnell, “SIC-POVMs from Stark units: Prime dimensions n^2+3”, arXiv:2112.05552 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1807.05877](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05877).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05552

record.title: The Torelli conjecture for mirror Landau–Ginzburg models
record.statement:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be Fano varieties with mirror Landau–Ginzburg models $(X_1^\vee,W_1)$ and $(X_2^\vee,W_2)$. Write $\pi_{W_i}(t)$ for the classical period of the model, and let $\widehat{G}_{X_i}(t)$ denote the corresponding regularized quantum period. **The Torelli conjecture.** If

$$
\pi_{W_1}(t)=\pi_{W_2}(t)
$$

(or equivalently if $\widehat{G}_{X_1}(t)=\widehat{G}_{X_2}(t)$), then $X_1^\vee$ and $X_2^\vee$ are isomorphic. This reformulates the period conjecture as a Torelli statement: the period should determine the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model, although the claim is not established in the stated generality.
record.source_name: Wendelin Lutz, “Mirrors to Del Pezzo Surfaces and the Classification of T-Polygons”, arXiv:2112.08246 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08246

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Erdős–Purdy–Agarwal–Sharir conjecture on congruent simplices
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 4$, let $k\leq d$, and let $\mathrm{C}(d,k,n)$ denote the maximum, over all $k$-vertex simplices $S$ and all $n$-element sets $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, of the number of occurrences of a congruent copy of $S$ in $P$. **Erdős–Purdy–Agarwal–Sharir conjecture.**

For $d\geq 4$ and $k\leq d$ we have

$$
\mathrm{C}(d,k,n)=O_d(\min\{n^k,n^{d/2}\})
$$

if $d$ is even, and

$$
\mathrm{C}(d,k,n)=O_d(\min\{n^k,n^{d/2-1/6}\})
$$

if $d$ is odd.

This conjecture concerns the higher-dimensional generalisation of the unit-distance problem, where one counts congruent simplices rather than pairs at a fixed distance. The paper develops upper bounds using classical cutting techniques, while the conjectured estimates remain unresolved in general.
record.source_name: Nora Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “On the Erdős-Purdy problem and the Zarankiewitz problem for semialgebraic graphs”, arXiv:2112.10245 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10245

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Conjecture on unit simplices in diameter graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{DIAM}(d,k,n)$ be the maximum number of unit $k$-simplices spanned by an $n$-point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ of diameter $1$. **Conjecture on unit simplices in diameter graphs.** For $d\geq 2$ and $k\leq d$ we have

$$
\mathrm{DIAM}(d,k,n)=O_d(\min\{n^k,n^{d-k+1}\}),
$$

and, for odd $d$ and $k=(d+1)/2$, we have

$$
\mathrm{DIAM}(d,k,n)=O_d(n^{k-1}).
$$

A theorem in the paper proves the weaker general bound $O_{d,\varepsilon}(n^{d/2+\varepsilon})$, so the conjecture is confirmed only up to a small error term in the stated setting. The sharper estimates remain open.
record.source_name: Nora Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “On the Erdős-Purdy problem and the Zarankiewitz problem for semialgebraic graphs”, arXiv:2112.10245 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10245

record.title: Verstraëte's girth-six conjecture for independent domination in cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $i(G)$ denote its independent domination number, the minimum size of an independent dominating set of $G$. The **girth** of $G$ is the length of a shortest cycle in $G$.

**Verstraëte's conjecture.** If $G$ is a cubic graph with girth at least $6$, then

$$
i(G) \leq \frac{|V(G)|}{3}.
$$

This conjecture seeks a sharper upper bound for independent domination in cubic graphs when short cycles, and in particular the complete bipartite extremal examples, are excluded. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Ilkyoo Choi, Hyemin Kwon and Boram Park, “Tight bound for independent domination of cubic graphs without 4-cycles”, arXiv:2112.11720 (2021).

record.title: Best-fit Stiefel tropical linear space at the Gaussian center
record.statement:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_d$ be independent random variables with distribution $N(0,\sigma^2)$, and regard $(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ as a point of $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}/\mathbb{R}\mathbf{1}$. Let $L_P$ be the Stiefel tropical linear space associated with $P$, and let the tropical distance be denoted by $d_{\rm tr}$.

**Best-fit Stiefel tropical linear space conjecture.** As $\sigma\to0$, the quantity

$$
\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[d_{\rm tr}((X_1,\ldots,X_d),L_P)\right]}{\sigma}
$$

achieves its minimum when $P=0$.

This is presented as the paper's ultimate goal for best-fitting non-hyperplane Stiefel tropical linear spaces. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Keiji Miura and Ruriko Yoshida, “Plücker Coordinates of the best-fit Stiefel Tropical Linear Space to a Mixture of Gaussian Distributions”, arXiv:2112.11893 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11893

record.title: Recursive 2-extension conjecture for extremal square-rich point sets
record.statement:
Let $S_{\square}(n)$ be the maximum number of squares determined by an $n$-point set in the plane, and let $\mathcal{P}_{4,1}^1$ denote the starting configuration consisting of a unit square. An $n$-point set is obtained by **recursive $2$-extension** if it is constructed from this configuration by repeatedly applying the $2$-extension operation. **Recursive 2-extension conjecture.** For $n\ge 6$, every $n$-point set $\mathcal{P}$ with

$$
S_{\square}(\mathcal{P})=S_{\square}(n)
$$

is similar to an $n$-point set $\mathcal{P}'$ obtained by recursive $2$-extension starting from $\mathcal{P}_{4,1}^1$. This would classify all extremal square-rich point sets up to similarity, despite the possible non-rigidity of recursively constructed configurations.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz, “Plane point sets with many squares or isosceles right triangles”, arXiv:2112.12716 (2021).

record.title: The four-color conjecture for odd colorings of planar graphs of girth at least six
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let the **girth** of $G$ be the length of its shortest cycle. Let $\chi_o(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a proper coloring of $G$ such that every non-isolated vertex has a color appearing an odd number of times in its open neighborhood.

**Girth-six odd-coloring conjecture.** Every planar graph $G$ of girth at least $6$ has

$$
\chi_o(G)\leq 4.
$$

The paper notes that many planar graphs of girth five require five colors for an odd coloring, motivating the stronger bound for girth at least six. The statement remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Mirko Petruševski and Riste Škrekovski, “Colorings with neighborhood parity condition”, arXiv:2112.13710 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: The quadratic diameter conjecture for friends-and-strangers graphs on cycles
record.statement:
Let $Y$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathsf{FS}(\textsf{Cycle}_n,Y)$ denote its friends-and-strangers graph. The **quadratic diameter conjecture** asserts that the maximum diameter of a connected component of

$$
\mathsf{FS}(\textsf{Cycle}_n,Y)
$$

is $O(n^2)$. This would sharpen the paper's polynomial diameter bound for cycles; the conjecture is presented as an unresolved improvement, and would imply an $O(n^3)$ bound for the corresponding double-flip distances.
record.source_name: Ryan Jeong, “On the Diameters of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs”, arXiv:2201.00665 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.00665

record.title: Sharpness conjecture for odd colorings of sparse graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{mad}(G)$ denote the maximum average degree of $G$, and let $\chi_o(G)$ be the smallest number of colors admitting an odd coloring of $G$. Fix $\epsilon$ such that $0<\epsilon\le 8/5$. **Sharpness conjecture.** If

$$
\mathrm{mad}(G)\le 4-\epsilon,
$$

then

$$
\chi_o(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{8}{\epsilon}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

The source says that this construction is suspected to be sharp, but supplies no resolution evidence; the claim is therefore recorded as open.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, “Odd Colorings of Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2201.01455 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01455

record.title: Maximum-curvature conjecture for optimal control of moving sets
record.statement: Let $\Omega(t)$ be the evolving set with boundary parametrized by $x(t,\xi)$, and let the optimal control be the normal velocity control acting along this boundary. Denote the curvature of the boundary at $x(t,\xi)$ by $\omega(t,\xi)$. **Maximum-curvature conjecture.** At every time $t\in[0,T]$, the optimal control is active precisely along the portion of the boundary where the curvature is maximum. This claim describes the geometric localization of the optimal control suggested by the backward dual equation: characteristics with larger curvature cause the dual variable to grow faster backward in time, making those boundary portions the most advantageous locations for shrinking the set. The parser provides no evidence that the claim has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Alberto Bressan, Maria Teresa Chiri and Najmeh Salehi, “Optimal Control of Moving Sets”, arXiv:2201.01723 (2022).

record.title: Scattering rigidity conjecture for compact Riemannian manifolds of Anosov type
record.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be compact Riemannian manifolds of Anosov type, each with scattering data. **Scattering rigidity conjecture.** If $M_1$ and $M_2$ have the same scattering data, then they are isometric by an isometry fixing the boundary. This conjecture proposes that scattering data determine a compact Riemannian manifold of Anosov type up to an isometry that fixes the boundary, extending the chain of rigidity implications discussed in the paper. Its resolution is not established in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Yannick Guedes Bonthonneau, Colin Guillarmou and Malo Jézéquel, “Scattering rigidity for analytic metrics”, arXiv:2201.02100 (2024).

record.title: Fractional-statistics emergence conjecture for quasihole tracer particles
record.statement:
Fix an integer $n\ge 2$. Let $p,\mu\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathfrak{b}=N\in\mathbb{N}$, and define

$$
\Psi_{\rm qh}(\mathbf{w};\mathbf{z})=\left(\prod_{j=1}^n\prod_{k=1}^N(w_j-z_k)^p\right)\left(\prod_{1\leq k<\ell\leq N}(z_k-z_\ell)^\mu\prod_{k=1}^N e^{-\mathfrak{b}|z_k|^2/2}\right).
$$

Let $\Phi\in C^0(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ have support in $\{ |x|\leq d\}^{\times n}$ for some $d<\sqrt{\mu}$, and assume that for some $C_\Phi>0$ and $\beta>0$,

$$
|\Phi(\mathbf{y})|\leq C_\Phi |y_i-y_j|^\beta
$$

for all $i\ne j$. For any $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, and for sufficiently large $\kappa>0$, define

$$
\mathbf{A}^{\rm tot}_j(\mathbf{y})=-\left(q-\frac{p}{\mu}\right)\mathfrak{b}y_j^\perp-\frac{p^2}{\mu}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\frac{(y_j-y_\ell)^\perp}{|y_j-y_\ell|^2}.
$$

**Fractional-statistics emergence conjecture.** As $N\to+\infty$, the identity

$$
\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2(N+n)}}\left|\left(-\mathrm{i}\nabla_{y_j}-q\mathfrak{b}y_j^\perp\right)\Psi_\Phi\right|^2=2\mathfrak{b}\frac{p}{\mu}+\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}\left|\left(-\mathrm{i}\nabla_{y_j}+\mathbf{A}^{\rm tot}_j(\mathbf{y})\right)\Phi\right|^2+\mathrm{Errors}
$$

should hold. This conjecture extends the paper's statistics-transmutation result from integer to fractional statistics, motivated by the fractional quantum Hall effect; the notation $\Psi_\Phi$ is inherited from the preceding definition in the paper, and the source does not state a quantified form of the error term.
record.source_name: Gaultier Lambert, Douglas Lundholm and Nicolas Rougerie, “Quantum statistics transmutation via magnetic flux attachment”, arXiv:2201.03518 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.03518

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: The product formula conjecture for maximum $(t,s)$-families
record.statement:
Let $t$ and $s$ be positive integers. A family $mathcal F\subset 2^{[n]}$ is a $(t,s)$-family if every two members satisfy $|A\cap B|\ge t$ and $|A\cup B|\le n-s$. Define

$$
m(n,t)=\max\{|\mathcal F|:\mathcal F\subset 2^{[n]}\text{ is }t\text{-intersecting}\},
$$

and let $m(n,t,s)$ be the maximum size of a $(t,s)$-family in $2^{[n]}$.

**Product formula conjecture.** If $n\ge t+s$, then

$$
m(n,t,s)=\max\bigl\{m(n',t)m(n-n',s):t\le n'\le n-s\bigr\}.
$$

The formula would determine the extremal size of every $(t,s)$-family from the corresponding one-sided intersection maxima. The surrounding discussion records the related inequality $m(n+n',t,s)\ge m(n,t)m(n',s)$, but gives no resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “Perfect matchings in down-sets”, arXiv:2201.03865 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.03865

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Exponential Time Hypothesis
record.statement:
There is no $2^{o(n)}$-time algorithm which can determine whether a given 3SAT formula on $n$ variables is satisfiable.

**Exponential Time Hypothesis.** There is no $2^{o(n)}$-time algorithm which can determine whether a given 3SAT formula on $n$ variables is satisfiable.

This hypothesis is used to establish the quasipolynomial lower bound for planning in observable POMDPs; its status is open and it formalizes the conjectured absence of subexponential-time algorithms for 3SAT.

record.title: Symmetry conjecture for an optimal pair in the minimum overlap problem
record.statement:
Let $f(x)$ and $M(x)$ be a pair of functions as in the source's formulation of the minimum overlap problem, let $\|M\|_{\infty}$ denote the supremum norm of $M$, and let $\mu$ be the minimum overlap constant. A pair is **symmetric** when both $f(x)$ and $M(x)$ have the symmetry used in the problem. **Symmetry conjecture.** There exists a pair of symmetric functions $f(x),M(x)$ as in the source's formulation such that

$$
\|M\|_{\infty}=\mu.
$$

If true, this would justify simplifying the convex program by imposing symmetry, because the relevant sine Fourier coefficients and $E(M)$ then vanish. The source uses the conjecture to derive a stronger computational lower bound for $\mu$, but does not report a proof or disproof.

record.title: Zeon formulation of Ryser's conjecture I
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be the zeon incidence representation of an $r$-uniform $r$-partite hypergraph. Let $\gamma$ be the zeon element

$$
\gamma=\sum_{\{I: \zeta_I\Gamma=0\}}\zeta_I.
$$

Here $\natural\gamma$ denotes the minimum grade of $\gamma$, and $\kappa(\Gamma)$ denotes the index of nilpotency of $\Gamma$.

**Zeon formulation of Ryser's conjecture I.** One has

$$
\natural\gamma\leq (r-1)(\kappa(\Gamma)-1).
$$

This is presented as an equivalent zeon-algebra formulation of Ryser's conjecture, and is open together with the underlying hypergraph conjecture.
record.source_name: Samuel Ewing and G. Stacey Staples, “Zeon and Idem-Clifford Formulations of Hypergraph Problems”, arXiv:2201.05895 (2022).

record.title: Bounded unit-hypercube dimension implies vanishing information rate
record.statement:
Let $\{P_i\}$ be an infinite family of toric codes. For an integral convex polytope $P$, define $M(P)$ to be the largest integer $j$ such that, after a unimodular affine transformation, the unit hypercube $[0,1]^j$ is contained in $P$.

**Bounded-hypercube conjecture.** If the sequence $\{M(P_i)\}$ is bounded, then

$$
R(P_i)\to 0\quad\text{as }i\to\infty.
$$

The paper has already shown that unbounded $M(P_i)$ forces the relative minimum distance to tend to zero. Thus this conjecture would rule out good families in the complementary bounded-hypercube case.
record.source_name: Mallory Dolorfino, Cordelia Horch, Kelly Jabbusch and Ryan Martinez, “On Good Infinite Families of Toric Codes or the Lack Thereof”, arXiv:2201.08464 (2024).

record.title: The directed Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture for branchings
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph. Write $\gamma(D)$ for the fractional arboricity of its underlying graph, and let $\Delta^-(D)$ and $\Delta^+(D)$ denote its maximum in-degree and maximum out-degree, respectively. A **branching** is a spanning subdigraph whose components are arborescences. **The directed Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture.** For positive integers $k$ and $d$, if

$$
\gamma(D) \leq k+\frac{d-k}{d+1},\qquad \Delta^-(D)\leq k+1,
$$

then $D$ decomposes into $k+1$ branchings $B_1,\ldots,B_k,B_{k+1}$ such that

$$
\Delta^+(B_{k+1})\leq d.
$$

This is proposed as the directed analogue of the Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Hui Gao and Daqing Yang, “Digraph analogues for the Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture”, arXiv:2201.10791 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10791

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Nielsen realization for aspherical closed manifolds with hyperbolic fundamental group
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an aspherical closed manifold with hyperbolic fundamental group $\pi$. Let $j\colon G\to \operatorname{Out}(\pi)$ be an embedding of a finite group $G$ into the outer automorphism group of $\pi$. Let $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ denote the group of self-homeomorphisms of $M$, and let $\nu\colon \operatorname{Aut}(M)\to \operatorname{Out}(\pi)$ be the canonical map induced by the action on the fundamental group. **Nielsen realization conjecture.** There is an effective topological $G$-action $\rho\colon G\to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$ on $M$ such that

$$
\nu\circ\rho=j.
$$

This asserts that every finite subgroup of the outer automorphism group of a hyperbolic fundamental group is realized by an effective topological action on the corresponding aspherical closed manifold. The source notes that, to the authors' knowledge, there is no counterexample; the general status is not established here.
record.source_name: Wolfgang Lueck, “On Brown's Problem, Poincare' models for the classifying spaces for proper actions and Nielsen Realization”, arXiv:2201.10807 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10807

record.title: The forcing-absoluteness conjecture for non-isomorphic Borel quotients
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal M}$ and ${\mathcal N}$ be Borel structures, discrete or metric, of the same signature. Let $E$ and $F$ be Borel congruences on ${\mathcal M}$ and ${\mathcal N}$, respectively.

**Non-isomorphism absoluteness conjecture.** If ${\mathcal M}/E$ and ${\mathcal N}/F$ are non-isomorphic in some forcing extension, then they are non-isomorphic in every forcing extension satisfying Martin's Maximum (MM).

This is a forcing-absoluteness assertion about quotient structures. The supplied status evidence says that all many instances in which it has been confirmed require only $\mathrm{OCA}_T$ and MA, so the conjecture is treated as solved in the database.
record.source_name: Ilijas Farah, Saeed Ghasemi, Andrea Vaccaro and Alessandro Vignati, “Corona Rigidity”, arXiv:2201.11618 (2025).

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Neumann–Lara's planar graph dichromatic conjecture
record.statement:
An **orientation** of a graph is obtained by assigning one of the two possible directions to each edge, and the **dichromatic number** of a digraph is the minimum number of colors needed so that every color class induces an acyclic subdigraph. A planar graph is a graph that can be embedded in the plane without crossings.

**Neumann–Lara's conjecture.** Every orientation of a planar graph has dichromatic number at most $2$.

This is a central open problem concerning dichromatic number, independently raised by Neumann–Lara and Škrekovski. It asks whether every planar graph remains 2-colorable into acyclic color classes under every orientation.
record.source_name: János Barát and Mátyás Czett, “The horizon of 2-dichromatic oriented graphs”, arXiv:2201.13161 (2022).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1708.02441](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02441), [arXiv:1510.03578](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.03578).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13161

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Four's a Crowd conjecture for eigenvector dispersion
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 6$ vertices. Write $P_{n-3}K_4$ for the kite graph consisting of a path attached to a complete graph $K_4$, and let $c_e(G)$ denote the eigenvector dispersion of $G$. **Four's a Crowd conjecture.** The connected graph which achieves the maximum of $c_e$ on $n\geq 6$ vertices is $P_{n-3}K_4$. This conjecture specifies the proposed extremal kite graph for eigenvector dispersion; the surrounding discussion notes that related extremal graph problems have different optimal head sizes, but gives no resolution of this claim.
record.source_name: Gregory J. Clark, “Comparing Eigenvector and Degree Dispersion with the Principal Ratio of a Graph”, arXiv:2202.00325 (2022).

record.title: Dijoin weight decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(D=(V,A),w)$ be a weighted digraph, and let $\tau$ be the minimum weight of a dicut, with $\tau\geq 3$.

**Dijoin weight decomposition conjecture.** There exist weighted digraphs $(D,c)$ and $(D,c')$ such that

$$
w=c+c',
$$

the minimum weight of a dicut in $(D,c)$ is $1$, and the minimum weight of a dicut in $(D,c')$ is $\tau-1$.

The source proposes this as a fix to the refuted Edmonds–Giles conjecture and states that it would imply the weighted dijoin-clutter $\tau=2$ conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ahmad Abdi, Gérard Cornuéjols and Michael Zlatin, “On packing dijoins in digraphs and weighted digraphs”, arXiv:2202.00392 (2023).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Pippenger–Golumbic's inducibility conjecture for cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the cycle graph on $k$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{I}(C_k)$ be its inducibility, the limiting maximum proportion of induced copies of $C_k$ in graphs with an increasing number of vertices. For $k\geq 5$, **Pippenger–Golumbic's inducibility conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{I}(C_k)=\dfrac{k!}{k^{k}-k}.
$$

The conjecture gives the exact inducibility of every cycle of length at least five. The source states that Pippenger and Golumbic conjectured this lower bound and showed that it is tight for this family of graphs.
record.source_name: Su Yuan Chan, Kerri Morgan and Julien Ugon, “Bounds On The Inducibility Of Double Loop Graphs”, arXiv:2202.00411 (2022).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2010.11664](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11664), [arXiv:1702.07342](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07342).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00411

record.title: Johansson's uniqueness conjecture for the parabolically shifted Airy process
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the Airy process, and consider the parabolically shifted process $x\mapsto\mathcal{A}(x)-x^2$.

**Johansson's conjecture.** Almost surely, $x\mapsto\mathcal{A}(x)-x^2$ attains its maximum at a unique point $Y\in\mathbb{R}$.

This conjecture concerns the uniqueness of the maximizer governing the scaling limit of a point-to-line geodesic in geometric last passage percolation. It was proved by Corwin and Hammond, with alternate proofs by Pimentel and by Flores and collaborators.
record.source_name: Duncan Dauvergne, “Non-uniqueness times for the maximizer of the KPZ fixed point”, arXiv:2202.01700 (2022).

record.title: Drury's partition-support conjecture for Schur power eigenvalues
record.statement: Let $\Pi$ be a partition of $n$, and let its Ferrers diagram be the associated diagram. For $A\in{\cal H}_n$, let the block of the Schur power matrix $\pi(A)$ associated with $\Pi$ be the block indexed by the corresponding irreducible representation of $\mathcal{S}_n$. **Drury's partition-support conjecture.** If the Ferrers diagram of $\Pi$ contains neither the Ferrers diagram of $(3,2)$ nor that of $(7,1)$, then the largest eigenvalue of the block associated with $\Pi$ is at most $\mathop{\rm per} A$. The source presents this as an open conjecture.

record.references:

record.title: Mathon and van Trung's conjecture on perfect sequence covering arrays
record.statement:
For integers $n$ and $k$, let $g(n,k)$ be the minimum covering multiplicity for a perfect sequence covering array with parameters $(n,k)$. The previously known exceptional values include $k=2$ and, by Mathon's construction, $k=4$. **Mathon and van Trung's conjecture.** If $k\notin\{2,4\}$, then

$$
g(k+2,k)>1.
$$

This revised conjecture isolates $k=4$ as the only possible additional value at which Levenshtein's conjecture fails. It is presented here without a resolution status; related computer results establish $g(7,4)>1$, $g(7,5)>1$, and $g(8,6)>1$.

record.title: Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum coloring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of planar graphs. Write $\chi_{\mathrm{pCFo}}$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{pUMc}}$ for the proper conflict-free chromatic number with respect to open neighborhoods and the proper unique-maximum chromatic number with respect to closed neighborhoods, respectively.

**Proper coloring conjecture.** For the class of planar graphs $\mathcal{P}$,

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{pCFo}}(\mathcal{P})=6\quad\text{and}\quad \chi_{\mathrm{pUMc}}(\mathcal{P})=6.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the current lower bounds are tight in these two proper-coloring cases; the paper leaves the corresponding upper bounds unresolved.
record.source_name: Igor Fabrici, Borut Lužar, Simona Rindošová and Roman Soták, “Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum colorings of planar graphs with respect to neighborhoods”, arXiv:2202.02570 (2022).

record.title: Brualdi–Quinn Massey's strong chromatic index conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $(a,b)$-bipartite graph, meaning that the two vertex classes of $G$ have maximum degrees at most $a$ and $b$, respectively. **Brualdi–Quinn Massey's conjecture.** The strong chromatic index satisfies

$$
\chi'_s(G)\leq ab.
$$

This conjecture refines the earlier conjecture of Faudree, Gyárfás, Schelp, and Tuza that every bipartite graph $G$ satisfies $\chi'_s(G)\leq \Delta(G)^2$. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.

record.title: Krenn–Gu conjecture on the matching index
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected graph with an even number of vertices. For an edge-colouring $c$, let $\mu(G,c)$ be the dimension achieved by a perfectly monochromatic edge-coloured graph, and let $\mu(G)$ be the maximum of $\mu(G,c)$ over all such colourings.

**Krenn–Gu conjecture.** If $G$ is non-isomorphic to $K_4$, then

$$
\mu(G)\leq 2
$$

and

$$
\mu(K_4)=3.
$$

The conjecture would show that $K_4$ is the unique graph, up to isomorphism, with matching index at least $3$, thereby ruling out higher-dimensional GHZ-state constructions from other finite graphs. The paper presents this as an open problem and later proves the corresponding characterization in the unweighted setting.

record.title: Boundedness of minimal log discrepancies of Kollár components with positive local volume
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}^*$, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $I\subseteq [0,1]\cap\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite set. For an $n$-dimensional klt pair $(X,\Delta)$ with $\operatorname{Coef}(\Delta)\subseteq I$ and a point $\eta\in X$, not necessarily closed, assume

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(\eta,X,\Delta)\geq \varepsilon.
$$

**Boundedness conjecture.** There exists a constant $A=A(n,\varepsilon,I)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{mld}^{\mathrm{K}}(\eta,X,\Delta)\leq A.
$$

Here $\operatorname{mld}^{\mathrm{K}}$ is the smallest log discrepancy among Kollár components over $\eta$. The paper proves this in dimensions at most three and shows that, in any dimension, it implies the boundedness conjecture for klt singularities with normalized volume bounded below.
record.source_name: Ziquan Zhuang, “On boundedness of singularities and minimal log discrepancies of Kollár components”, arXiv:2202.06455 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06455

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Boundedness of minimal log discrepancies of Kollár components
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}^*$ and let $I\subseteq [0,1]\cap\mathbb{Q}$ be a DCC set. For a klt pair $(X,\Delta)$ with $\operatorname{Coef}(\Delta)\subseteq I$ and a point $\eta\in X$ of codimension $n$, define $\operatorname{mld}^{\mathrm{K}}(\eta,X,\Delta)$ as the smallest log discrepancy among Kollár components over $\eta$.

**Boundedness conjecture.** There exists a constant $A=A(n,I)$, depending only on $n$ and $I$, such that

$$
\operatorname{mld}^{\mathrm{K}}(\eta,X,\Delta)\leq A.
$$

This is proposed as a stronger analogue of the boundedness conjecture for minimal log discrepancies. The paper verifies related special cases, including codimension two, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Ziquan Zhuang, “On boundedness of singularities and minimal log discrepancies of Kollár components”, arXiv:2202.06455 (2023).

record.title: Bounded Weil index of K-semistable Fano varieties
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}^*$. For an $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano variety $X$, define its Weil index as the largest integer $q$ such that $-K_X\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}qA$ for some Weil divisor $A$.

**Weil-index boundedness conjecture.** There exists a constant $N>0$ depending only on $n$ such that the Weil index of every $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano variety is at most $N$.

This would give a uniform dimensional bound on the Weil indices of K-semistable Fano varieties. The paper presents it as a stronger statement motivated by the boundedness conjecture for minimal log discrepancies of Kollár components; it remains open.
